hypothesis: Some range overclaims occur because strict-envelope returns are discarded by edge confidence margins, point-count thresholds or infrastructure classification before clear_cap. Representing every physical-profile return as unresolved evidence may remove these overclaims; its cost on empty data must be measured, not waived.
prior_work: 25Sep clear_cap C0 used third nearest corridor return after confidence margins and removed some overclaims but reduced median empty/ride range by more than its limit. M1 is the first-return limit before confidence margins, including returns never clustered; it is expected to be more conservative and may be rejected. No threshold sweep follows.
implementation: Read-only Detector subclass snapshots corridor_mask strict geometric membership before gauge_core margins and low stage. After unchanged detector process, cap estimated range at the nearest raw strict-envelope point within existing gauge range. If this shortens clear_distance by >0.5m, mark monitoring unknown/CAUTION on non-STOP and non-FAULT frames. STOP detections, tracking, geometry and all upstream processing remain byte-identical. No column exemptions, label use, fitted-label feedback or selective object cases.

gates.upstream_detection_output: identical to frozen baseline except informational timing
gates.diagnostic_limit: Stored envelope labels come from an earlier fitted model, not surveyed truth; zero diagnostic overclaims alone cannot certify free track.

sequence: Evaluate frozen detector plus observer on setO and five emptyrecordings first. If either overclaim or emptycost condition fails, reject M1 without full ride/gate expenditure; preserve complete observed results. If these pass, run ride, full diagnosticcomparison and independent review before considering production code.
on_failure: No ship and no retuning; use exact observed failure to guide future model/evidence research.
